name: com.coveragecat/insurance
title: Coverage Cat
description: Estimate personal umbrella costs, compare standalone policies, or check an existing policy.

tools.name: umbrella_consumer_prefill
tools.description: Start a comparison of available personal umbrella policies, including standalone options that may let the shopper keep their current auto insurer. Use when the shopper asks to compare policies, get quotes, or buy coverage; availability depends on the household and insurer. For a price-range question without a shopping request, use umbrella_calculator. This consumer shopping entry point does not require an operator bearer token. On a cold start, call this before asking the shopper a questionnaire and assemble the fullest justified estimate from user-controlled context. Use canonical umbrella keys such as address.street/city/state/zip, license_state, license_number, approximate_asset_value or net_worth_numeric, desired_coverage_limit, required_coverage_e_limit, and vehicle_count or umbrella_details.motorized_vehicle_count. Do not send vehicles rows before submission. Stay on the same consumer-operated subset through `consumer_intake_issues`, `consumer_intake_patch`, `umbrella_consumer_select`, `umbrella_consumer_bind`, `umbrella_consumer_attach`, `umbrella_consumer_payment`, `umbrella_consumer_policy`, and `umbrella_consumer_service`. If you are rehearsing the shopper flow, set `sandbox: true` on this first prefill call only. That same consumer sandbox uid can then continue through the same shopper-safe flow. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Until later follow-up shows progress, tell the shopper the application is not submitted yet. Coverage Cat will not resume or expose a prior consumer umbrella draft based on email alone. Continue an existing consumer draft only through the issued uid plus the current hidden MCP session or latest intake_access_token handoff.

acquisition_campaign.description: Optional public campaign code supplied in the shopper's starting prompt. Copy it only when supplied; do not infer it or send personal information. It does not change eligibility or pricing.

credit_consent_pending.description: Declares that this handoff starts before the shopper has given consumer-report authorization for insurance underwriting, so do not ask about it now. Coverage Cat requests that authorization on `umbrella_consumer_select`, once the shopper picks an offer.

field_estimates.description: Provenance for intake values you inferred from context rather than heard from the shopper, one row per inferred value. On the initial umbrella handoff, add rows only for fields that already appear in the current umbrella review; otherwise send `intake` alone.

confidence.description: How strongly your source supports the inferred value.

field.description: Intake dot-path of the inferred value, matching the key you sent under `intake`, such as `address.zip`.

source.description: Free-form label for where the inferred value came from, such as `policy_declarations`, `email_thread`, or a property-data provider.

idempotency_key.description: Key you generate to identify one logical umbrella_consumer_prefill request, so a retry cannot apply it twice. After a timeout or transport failure, retry with the same key and identical arguments to get the original result back; Coverage Cat keeps that result for 24 hours and rejects different arguments sent under a used key.

intake.description: Fullest currently known consumer umbrella application patch. Use canonical keys such as address.street/city/state/zip, license_state, license_number, approximate_asset_value or net_worth_numeric, desired_coverage_limit, required_coverage_e_limit, and vehicle_count or umbrella_details.motorized_vehicle_count for umbrella counts. Do not send vehicles rows before submission.

current_auto_coverages.description: Which band the shopper's current underlying auto liability limits fall into: `500k/1m` covers $500k/$1 Million/$100k or higher; `500k/500k` covers $500k/$500k/$100k or $500k CSL; `300k/300k` covers $250k/$500k/$100k or $300k/$300k/$100k or $300k CSL; `100k/300k` covers $100k/$300k/$100k or lower. Pick the strongest band the shopper's actual limits fully satisfy. Underlying auto limits gate umbrella eligibility, so use `unsure` only when the shopper genuinely does not know their limits.

sandbox.description: Set true on this first prefill call to run a fully synthetic shopper rehearsal instead of a live application. The returned sandbox uid continues through the same consumer tool set.

tools.name: consumer_intake_issues
tools.description: Read the status of an umbrella application or an existing homeowners policy. Records request attribution and rotates follow-up access. In the umbrella sandbox, polling advances checkout and can create a synthetic policy; it does not issue real coverage. Returns the intake's status and detail_status, whether the application is submitted, the staged review and next_question, quoted offers with their selection_token, and any post-choose, payment, policy, or conversation state. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Stay on the default consumer-operated subset and, before submission, say explicitly that the application is not submitted yet. For umbrella, keep missing fields hidden until Coverage Cat stages the single pre-submit review turn, then ask only for the explicitly missing shopper-owned fields in `next_question` and invite corrections instead of re-keying reviewed values. Coverage Cat will not resume or expose a prior consumer umbrella draft based on email alone. Continue an existing consumer draft only through the issued uid plus the current hidden MCP session or latest intake_access_token handoff. Normalize shopper birthdays from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD before you patch Coverage Cat.

intake_access_token.description: Send the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. Required for stateless MCP 2026-07-28 requests; also accepted by legacy hosts. Keep it private and never show it to the shopper.

uid.description: Coverage Cat intake uid for the existing authorized intake or returned by `umbrella_consumer_prefill` and echoed on every follow-up response. Reuse it for each follow-up call on the same application.

tools.name: consumer_intake_verify_email
tools.description: When consumer_intake_issues reports verification.required, ask the shopper whether to send a verification email, then call with confirm_send: true. The link goes only to the application's email on file. Ask the shopper to open it, then poll consumer_intake_issues until verification.required is false. Never ask the shopper to paste the login link or code into chat.

confirm_send.description: Confirm that the shopper asked to send a verification link to their application's email on file.

idempotency_key.description: Key you generate to identify one logical consumer_intake_verify_email request, so a retry cannot apply it twice. After a timeout or transport failure, retry with the same key and identical arguments to get the original result back; Coverage Cat keeps that result for 24 hours and rejects different arguments sent under a used key.

tools.name: consumer_intake_patch
tools.description: Patch or submit a consumer-prefill umbrella handoff, or reply to existing-policy support correspondence in chat. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Stay on the default consumer-operated subset. For umbrella, use the staged review turn to send only explicitly missing shopper-owned details plus corrections, set `confirm_submission` only on that final review confirmation, do not send vehicles rows on this pre-submit patch, and do not ask for umbrella credit consent here. Normalize shopper birthdays from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD, and tell the shopper the application is not submitted yet until you actually submit it. Returns the same follow-up payload as `consumer_intake_issues` for the updated intake.

tools.name: umbrella_consumer_select
tools.description: Continue the consumer-prefill umbrella flow after quotes are ready. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Stay on the same consumer-operated MCP subset, use the returned selection_token, collect the real user's consumer-report authorization for insurance underwriting here, and let Coverage Cat enter the normal post-choose workflow without switching to delegated tools. A selected Monoline offer also requires the separate returned MVR authorization; show its full text and source URL and collect both receipts in the same turn. If the quote payload exposed selection_guidance.same_reply_requirements for the chosen offer, send those answers under intake on this first select call. If Coverage Cat returns a consent-required response with a bind-stage next_question, ask for all returned authorizations and details together, then retry this same tool with the receipts and intake.

tools.name: umbrella_consumer_attach
tools.description: Upload declarations or auto declarations during the consumer-prefill umbrella post-choose flow. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Stay on the same consumer-operated MCP subset. Use only after selection and only when Coverage Cat says documents are needed. If both the home and auto files are already available, prefer one attach call with attachments so the shopper only approves one upload turn. If your runtime already has the files on disk or can stream raw bytes, prefer the REST binary `/api/intake/{uid}/attach-upload` fallback instead of hand-building base64. The upload itself is usually quick once the files are available, and secure checkout is usually ready about 5-10 minutes after Coverage Cat has the uploads on file.

filename.description: Original file name with its extension, such as `home-declarations.pdf`. Coverage Cat reads the file type from the extension and accepts PDF, JPEG, or PNG files.

type.description: Which policy the declarations page belongs to: `declarations` for the home, condo, renters, or landlord policy, or `auto_declarations` for the auto policy. Match the upload types Coverage Cat listed in `required_upload_types`.

tools.name: umbrella_consumer_payment
tools.description: Prepare secure Stripe payment collection or submit the resulting payment method during the consumer-prefill umbrella post-choose flow. Reuse uid and the latest intake_access_token from the previous successful Coverage Cat response on each follow-up. MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless and requires that token. Legacy MCP hosts may also preserve hidden shopper session authorization. Keep tokens private and stay on this same MCP follow-up tool. Stay on the same consumer-operated MCP subset. Use this only after Coverage Cat says payment_needed. First call it with payment_collection_requested: true; do not send the shopper straight to payment_url before you try this native step. If the host confirms the registered secure payment UI can render, display it and wait for completion; do not request card details through conversational text. After successful Stripe setup, call this same tool again with setup_intent_id and payment_method_id. If UI support is unknown or unsupported, or if secure setup fails in chat, share payment_url with the specific fallback reason instead.

inputSchema.description: Provide either payment_collection_requested: true or both setup_intent_id and payment_method_id, never both modes.

idempotency_key.description: Key you generate to identify one logical umbrella_consumer_payment request, so a retry cannot apply it twice. After a timeout or transport failure, retry with the same key and identical arguments to get the original result back; Coverage Cat keeps that result for 24 hours and rejects different arguments sent under a used key.

payment_collection_requested.description: Starts secure card collection: Coverage Cat prepares a Stripe SetupIntent and returns the publishable_key, client_secret, and setup_intent_id the registered payment UI needs. Send it on the first payment call, without setup_intent_id or payment_method_id.

payment_method_id.description: Reusable Stripe PaymentMethod id produced by secure client-side setup confirmation.

setup_intent_id.description: SetupIntent id returned by the earlier payment_collection_ready response.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send a bug report, suggestion, or purchase-flow problem to Coverage Cat's internal review queue at any stage. Send only feedback the user asked to share or an agent's own technical observation. Omit personal information, credentials, payment details, and transcripts. This does not change an application, request policy service, or authorize a purchase.

message.description: Describe the problem or suggestion. Omit personal information, credentials, payment details, and transcripts.

request_id.description: Optional UUID. Reuse it when retrying the same feedback to avoid duplicate notifications.

tool.description: Optional name of the tool or command involved.

tools.name: home_calculator
tools.description: Estimate annual and monthly home insurance ranges for a California property and return the normalized inputs, available risk-factor ids, and ZIP-level context notes that explain the estimate.

home_sqft.description: Approximate finished living area of the home in square feet.

risk_factors.description: Optional Coverage Cat risk-factor ids, such as `pool` or `old_systems`, for property traits that can change premium.

zip.description: ZIP code for the California property being estimated.

tools.name: umbrella_calculator
tools.description: Estimate how much personal umbrella insurance could cost: return annual price ranges using ZIP code and household details, with pricing factors. Read-only research; these estimates are not insurer quotes and do not start an application. For a request to compare standalone policies or shop for coverage, use umbrella_consumer_prefill.

antique_vehicles.description: How many collector or antique vehicles should be counted in the risk profile.

at_fault_accidents.description: Total at-fault accidents across all household drivers. Omitted counts as none; a high count can move the profile to specialized review or make it ineligible for instant pricing.

auto_count.description: How many cars, trucks, or SUVs are in the household auto profile.

drivers_over_70.description: Number of drivers in the household who are 70 or older.

drivers_under_22.description: Number of drivers in the household who are younger than 22.

jet_skis.description: Count of personal watercraft such as jet skis.

large_watercraft.description: Count of boats of any size; personal watercraft go under jet_skis.

motorcycles.description: How many motorcycles should be added to the total vehicle exposure.

moving_violations.description: Total moving violations across all household drivers. Omitted counts as none; a high count can move the profile to specialized review or make it ineligible for instant pricing.

property_count.description: How many residential properties the household owns or carries liability for.

zip.description: ZIP code for the household being priced.

tools.name: auto_estimates
tools.description: Estimate monthly auto premiums for one driver and vehicle profile across several carriers. Returns each carrier's id, name, and monthly premium spread (lowest, lower, median, upper, and highest modeled premium) in US dollars, plus the normalized inputs the model used. These are model estimates for research, not bindable quotes.

age.description: Age in years of the driver being priced; the model converts it to a birth year.

collision_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward a collision repair before collision coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

comprehensive_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward non-collision damage, such as theft, hail, or vandalism, before comprehensive coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

gender.description: Driver gender code the pricing model rates on: `M` for male, `F` for female, or `N` when not specified.

seed.description: Optional deterministic seed for the estimate sample when a caller wants stable repeat runs.

state.description: Two-letter state code for the garaging address or rating state.

style.description: Vehicle trim, body style, or submodel when you want to narrow the vehicle match.

year.description: Vehicle model year. With make and model it prices a specific car; omit it to price a generic vehicle instead.

zip.description: ZIP code for the driver or garaging location being priced.

tools.name: collision_and_comprehensive_coverage
tools.description: Estimate what collision and comprehensive coverage cost for one driver and vehicle profile, to help decide whether to carry them. Returns monthly premium spreads in US dollars with no physical-damage coverage, collision only, and both, plus collision-only and both after one claim, and cumulative premium projections for each coverage option over projection_years. These are model estimates, not bindable quotes.

age.description: Age in years of the driver being priced; the model converts it to a birth year.

collision_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward a collision repair before collision coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

comprehensive_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward non-collision damage, such as theft, hail, or vandalism, before comprehensive coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

gender.description: Driver gender code the pricing model rates on: `M` for male, `F` for female, or `N` when not specified.

seed.description: Optional deterministic seed for the estimate sample when a caller wants stable repeat runs.

state.description: Two-letter state code for the garaging address or rating state.

style.description: Vehicle trim, body style, or submodel when you want to narrow the vehicle match.

year.description: Vehicle model year. With make and model it prices a specific car; omit it to price a generic vehicle instead.

zip.description: ZIP code for the driver or garaging location being priced.

tools.name: file_a_claim
tools.description: Estimate whether filing an auto collision claim costs more than paying for the repair yourself. Returns monthly premium spreads with and without one claim, the monthly and multi-year premium increase, the collision deductible, the total cost of filing (deductible plus premium increase), and a file_claim or pay_out_of_pocket recommendation with the estimated savings. These are model estimates, not carrier quotes.

age.description: Age in years of the driver being priced; the model converts it to a birth year.

collision_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward a collision repair before collision coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

comprehensive_deductible.description: Dollars the driver pays toward non-collision damage, such as theft, hail, or vandalism, before comprehensive coverage pays the rest. Omitted means $1,000.

gender.description: Driver gender code the pricing model rates on: `M` for male, `F` for female, or `N` when not specified.

repair_estimate.description: Approximate dollar amount you expect to pay to repair the vehicle if you do not file a claim.

seed.description: Optional deterministic seed for the estimate sample when a caller wants stable repeat runs.

state.description: Two-letter state code for the garaging address or rating state.

style.description: Vehicle trim, body style, or submodel when you want to narrow the vehicle match.

year.description: Vehicle model year. With make and model it prices a specific car; omit it to price a generic vehicle instead.

zip.description: ZIP code for the driver or garaging location being priced.

tools.name: umbrella_limit_planner
tools.description: Compare how much umbrella coverage to consider from net worth, independently confirmed protected assets, an optional income allowance, and the lowest applicable underlying liability limit. Returns the arithmetic target, additional limit needed, and $0/$1M/$2M/$3M/$5M/$10M scenarios. This is planning, not a quote or a determination of legally exposed assets.

annual_income.description: Income included in your optional planning allowance. Whole US dollars.
annual_income.title: Annual household income

income_years.description: Choose 0 for an assets-only scenario; not a garnishment estimate.
income_years.title: Years of income to include

net_worth.description: Assets minus debts, including property equity. Use 0 if negative. Whole US dollars.
net_worth.title: Net worth

protected_assets.description: Only amounts included in net worth whose legal protection you have confirmed. Whole US dollars.
protected_assets.title: Legally protected assets

underlying_limit.description: Use the lowest applicable auto, home, or rental liability limit. For a single injured person under split auto limits, use the per-person limit. Do not add separate policies together. Whole US dollars.
underlying_limit.title: Applicable underlying liability limit

tools.name: umbrella_underlying_limit_check
tools.description: Check an auto, homeowners, renters, or rental-property policy against the underlying liability requirements stated in a specific umbrella quote. Supply requirements from that quote, not assumed carrier minimums. Missing current limits stay unknown. Returns each required increase separately; it does not determine claim payouts or eligibility.

current_limit.description: Read from your current declarations. Omit or use null if unknown; enter 0 only when confirmed. Whole US dollars.
current_limit.title: Current liability limit

current_per_accident.description: Read from your current declarations. Omit or use null if unknown; enter 0 only when confirmed. Whole US dollars. Must be at least the corresponding per-person limit.
current_per_accident.title: Current bodily injury per accident

current_per_person.description: Read from your current declarations. Omit or use null if unknown; enter 0 only when confirmed. Whole US dollars.
current_per_person.title: Current bodily injury per person

current_property_damage.description: Read from your current declarations. Omit or use null if unknown; enter 0 only when confirmed. Whole US dollars.
current_property_damage.title: Current property damage per accident

policy_type.description: Choose home for homeowners, renters, or rental-property liability; auto_csl for combined single limit; auto_split for separate bodily-injury and property-damage limits. auto_split requires required_per_person, required_per_accident, and required_property_damage; home and auto_csl require required_limit. Send only fields for the chosen structure.
policy_type.title: Policy limit structure

required_limit.description: Read the positive required limit from the specific umbrella quote or policy. Whole US dollars.
required_limit.title: Required liability limit

required_per_accident.description: Read the positive required limit from the specific umbrella quote or policy. Whole US dollars. Must be at least the corresponding per-person limit.
required_per_accident.title: Required bodily injury per accident

required_per_person.description: Read the positive required limit from the specific umbrella quote or policy. Whole US dollars.
required_per_person.title: Required bodily injury per person

required_property_damage.description: Read the positive required limit from the specific umbrella quote or policy. Whole US dollars.
required_property_damage.title: Required property damage per accident

tools.name: umbrella_bundle_comparison
tools.description: Compare the total cost of keeping existing home and auto insurance with standalone umbrella coverage versus moving all three to a bundle. Enter annual net premiums, required underlying-limit upgrades, and one-time switching cost. Returns first-year and multi-year totals, savings, and the first whole break-even year. Flags unverified coverage comparability; no carrier prices are invented.

auto_upgrade_premium.description: Additional annual cost to meet standalone umbrella requirements. Whole US dollars.
auto_upgrade_premium.title: Annual auto limit upgrade

bundled_auto_premium.description: Annual replacement auto quote, after discounts, with required limits. Double a six-month premium; multiply a monthly premium by 12. Whole US dollars.
bundled_auto_premium.title: Bundled auto premium

bundled_home_premium.description: Annual replacement home quote, after discounts, with required limits. Whole US dollars.
bundled_home_premium.title: Bundled home premium

bundled_umbrella_premium.description: Annual bundled umbrella quote at the same limit. Whole US dollars.
bundled_umbrella_premium.title: Bundled umbrella premium

coverage_comparable.description: True only after comparing limits, deductibles, exclusions, insured risks, and claims terms.
coverage_comparable.title: Coverage terms have been compared

current_auto_premium.description: Annual premium for the auto policies you would keep. Double a six-month premium; multiply a monthly premium by 12. Whole US dollars.
current_auto_premium.title: Current auto premium

current_home_premium.description: Annual premium for the home, renters, or rental policies you would keep. Whole US dollars.
current_home_premium.title: Current home premium

home_upgrade_premium.description: Additional annual cost to meet standalone umbrella requirements. Whole US dollars.
home_upgrade_premium.title: Annual home limit upgrade

standalone_umbrella_premium.description: Annual standalone umbrella quote at the limit you want. Whole US dollars.
standalone_umbrella_premium.title: Standalone umbrella premium

switching_cost.description: Additional nonrefundable cost of moving to the bundle; exclude refunded or overlapping premiums. Whole US dollars.
switching_cost.title: One-time switching cost

years.description: Assumes unchanged annual premiums across this period.
years.title: Years to compare

tools.name: docs_list_topics
tools.description: List Coverage Cat documentation topics from the same consumer MCP connection and return each topic's title, category, URI, MIME type, summary, and public href.

category.description: Docs category to browse: `developers` for guides such as quickstart, auth, sandbox, and MCP setup, `api` for discovery and OpenAPI documents, `skills` for runtime skill guides, or `all`. Omit it to browse every category.

limit.description: How many topics to return from the start of the filtered catalog. Omit it to get up to 25.

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search quickstart, auth, sandbox, OpenAPI, and runtime skill docs on this consumer MCP connection. Topics are ranked by how many query words appear in their title, summary, URI, or category; each match carries its title, category, URI, MIME type, summary, and public href, and an empty matches list means no topic contains any query word. Pass a match's uri to docs_get_resource to read it.

limit.description: How many of the best-ranked topics to return. Omit it to get the top 5.

query.description: Search terms describing the documentation need.

tools.name: docs_get_resource
tools.description: Read one Coverage Cat docs resource by URI from the default consumer MCP and return its URI, public href (null when it has no public page), MIME type, and full markdown, JSON, or YAML text.

uri.description: A coveragecat:// or ui:// resource URI from docs_list_topics or docs_search.
